components.gap: Durrett Example 3.2.5 (p. 117): two source claims are not supplied on the route or in the packet's owned files. (a) The interpretation that for N = 365, P(T_N > n) is the probability that two people in a group of size n do not have the same birthday, assuming all birthdays are equally likely: handbook/parts/p15/weak-convergence-of-laws.tex 392-407 states only the abstract model (independent uniform observations on {1,...,N}, first repeat index T_N), and handbook/annex/p15/weak-convergence-of-laws.tex 752-785 uses the word 'birthdays' and excludes nonuniform birth frequencies but never states this reading. (b) The source's comparison that the limit approximation P(T_365 > 22) ~ e^{-0.6630} ~ 0.515 is 2% smaller than the true probability 0.524: handbook/parts/p15/weak-convergence-of-laws.tex 405-407 gives the two values 0.524305 and 0.515296 but not the comparison (the exact relative shortfall is about 1.7%). Examples 3.2.2-3.2.4 and the rest of 3.2.5 (product formula, all m, the limit for x >= 0, the limiting CDF, the two numerical values) are present with complete proofs. Supply (a) and (b).
